sentences.text: Shri Sanjay Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the ap  Shri Hemant Sharma, learned Govt.Advocate for the re  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 483 of B.N.S.S., 2023 for grant of bail to the applicants/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.684/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Namli, District Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 366, 376(2)(n),
506, 190 of IPC.
2.

Prosecution story, in brief, is that 6.6.2021 when the prosecutrix was alone at her home,
co-accused Sanjay came in the house and after giving false pretext to marry her commit rape upon her.
He also repeated the aforesaid act several times, therefore, the prosecutrix got pregnant.
A girl child was born, but later on she died.
Lastly, the co-accused Sanjay denied to marry her.
The matter was reported by the prosecutrix on 4.12.2024.

Later on the prosecutrix also stated in her statement recorded under Section 164 of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:32081 2 MCRC-46730-2024 Cr.P.C. that present applicant and co-accused Pankaj forcibly took the prosecutrix to a room as a hotel, where co-accused Sanjay was also present.
All the accused persons threatened to kill her.
Thereafter, applicant and co- accused Pankaj left the prosecutrix and returned back.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that name of the applicant has not been mentioned in the FIR, which was lodged by the prosecutrix.
It is submitted that the matter was reported belatedly for around two and half years later of the incident without any plausible reasons, therefore, case of the prosecution is doubtful.
He is in custody since 14.10.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant -- Smt.Sona shall be released on bail upon furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for her appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during pendency NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:32081 3 MCRC-46730-2024 of the trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of B.N.S.S.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, the application is allowed and stands disposed off.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE patil Smt. Sona @ Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170031444/
